tasks.short: Inventory personal effects from the body.

steps.what: Inventory jewelry and wallets by hand.

tasks.design: The coroner recovers the effects and inventories jewelry and wallets by hand, then reviews the list. The file stores that inventory. It does not describe an item from a photo.
tasks.previous_blocker: Effects are small, similar, and easy to miscount once they leave the body.
tasks.enabler_now: An inventory the coroner has written and reviewed can be stored without a second count.
tasks.still_hard: A missing ring or a wallet counted twice becomes a dispute with the family.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner counts the items. The file holds the count they reviewed.
tasks.altitude: Recovering and counting the effects stay physical. The file holds the inventory the coroner reviewed.

reach.task: Receive effects listed on the inventory the coroner reviewed

evidence.claim: An inventory written by the coroner can be stored after they review it. The count itself stays in their hands.

Assigning cause or manner of death, certifying a death, and arranging care for a child are determinations the coroner makes. A tool does not make them. National rules decide who may certify a death. EU data-protection rules cover medical details and living relatives. The file stores only what the coroner recorded, and interviews are not stored as audio.

assumptions: The workflow starts when effects are recovered and ends when the reviewed inventory is on the file. Releasing the effects is a separate task.
The fields are case id, item, and count. The coroner produces them by counting. A photo is not turned into an item line.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on the recovery and the count. Only the copy of a reviewed inventory is shorter.
Upkeep is keeping the item labels, such as jewelry and wallet, stable.
unknowns: Whether a second person must watch the inventory.
Whether cash is counted separately from other effects.
research_questions: Must a second person watch the inventory?
Is cash counted separately from other effects?

already_counted.description: Inventorying jewelry and wallets stays in full inside that step

approvals.approved_version: inventory of effects the coroner reviewed after counting them

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the inventory is written once into the file while the items are still in hand, the second copy disappears and the low end is the recovery and the count, which stay. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct the workers on the examination.

steps.what: Review the direction given to workers.
File the note on the permanent records.

tasks.design: The coroner directs the workers who conduct the autopsy, the analyses, and the permanent records. A note of that direction is filed after they review it. The note is not a score of the worker, and no one is ranked.
tasks.previous_blocker: What the team should do next depends on what the body shows, which the coroner sees.
tasks.enabler_now: A direction the coroner has given and reviewed can be stored for the permanent record.
tasks.still_hard: An analysis done in the wrong order spoils the sample, and a score of a worker is a different decision that is not this task.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner directs the work. The file does not assign it and does not judge the worker.
tasks.altitude: Directing the autopsy, the analyses, and the records stays with the coroner. The file holds the direction they reviewed, not an evaluation.

reach.task: Carry out a direction the coroner gave
reach.learn: The coroner decided the order of the work

evidence.claim: A direction the coroner gave can be stored after they review it. The note does not score or rank a worker.

Assigning cause or manner of death, certifying a death, and arranging care for a child are determinations the coroner makes. A tool does not make them. National rules decide who may certify a death. EU data-protection rules cover medical details and living relatives. The file stores only what the coroner recorded, and interviews are not stored as audio.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the team is ready and ends when the reviewed direction is on the file. Doing the autopsy is a separate task.
The fields are case id, the work asked for, and who was asked. The coroner produces them by directing. No rating and no comparison of workers is stored.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on the direction. The note is a copy of a direction already given, not a judgement of the person.
Upkeep is keeping the work-type labels, such as autopsy and toxicology, stable.
unknowns: Which analyses this office runs itself and which it sends out.
Whether the direction note is part of the permanent record.
research_questions: Which analyses does this office run itself?
Is the direction note part of the permanent record?

already_counted.description: Directing workers conducting autopsies stays in full inside that step

approvals.approved_version: direction note the coroner reviewed after directing the workers

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the direction is spoken and rarely written, the low end is the directing itself, which stays. The note never becomes a score of a worker. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Release effects and arrange unclaimed remains.

steps.what: Identify authorized persons for a release.
Check the release against the inventory.

tasks.design: The coroner identifies the authorized person, releases the effects in person, and facilitates the disposition of unclaimed corpses. The file stores the release record only after they accept it. It does not choose the person or the disposition.
tasks.previous_blocker: Who is authorized, and what happens to an unclaimed body, are decisions under national rules and on the facts of the case.
tasks.enabler_now: A release the coroner has already made can be written into the file once.
tasks.still_hard: Releasing effects to the wrong person, or disposing of a body too soon, cannot be undone.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner decides the release and the disposition. The file records what they decided.
tasks.altitude: The release and the disposition stay with the coroner. The file holds the record they accepted after checking it against the inventory.

reach.learn: The coroner identified them and checked the inventory

evidence.claim: A release record can be stored after the coroner has identified the person and released the effects. It does not choose either.

Assigning cause or manner of death, certifying a death, and arranging care for a child are determinations the coroner makes. A tool does not make them. National rules decide who may certify a death. EU data-protection rules cover medical details and living relatives. The file stores only what the coroner recorded, and interviews are not stored as audio.

assumptions: The workflow starts when effects or a body can be released and ends when the accepted record is on the file. The inventory is a separate task.
The fields are case id, the authorized person, the items released, and the disposition the coroner facilitated. The coroner produces them. No person is suggested.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on the release and the disposition. Only the copy of an accepted record is shorter.
Upkeep is keeping the list of dispositions this office is allowed to use.
unknowns: Who counts as an authorized person under national rules.
How long an unclaimed body is kept before a disposition.
research_questions: Who counts as an authorized person under national rules?
How long is an unclaimed body kept?

already_counted.description: Facilitating disposition of unclaimed corpses stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the list of dispositions this office may use

approvals.approved_version: release record the coroner accepted after releasing the effects and checking the inventory

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If each release is still written by hand because the items differ, the low end is the identification, the release, the disposition, and the check, which stay. No person is chosen by a tool. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Witness and certify a judicial death.

steps.what: Witness the death under the judicial order.
Certify the death after the judicial order was witnessed.
File the wording used to certify the death.

tasks.design: The coroner witnesses the death under the judicial order and certifies it. The file stores that certification. It does not witness and it does not certify.
tasks.previous_blocker: The certification is of a particular death the coroner was present for, under a particular order.
tasks.enabler_now: The certification they have just made can be placed on the file without a second writing.
tasks.still_hard: Certifying a death the coroner did not witness would be false.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner witnesses and certifies. The file holds that certification.
tasks.altitude: Witnessing and certifying stay with the coroner. The file holds the certification they made after they witnessed the death.

reach.task: Receive a certification the coroner made
reach.learn: The coroner witnessed the death under the order

evidence.claim: A certification the coroner made after witnessing a death can be stored. The witnessing and the certifying stay theirs.

Assigning cause or manner of death, certifying a death, and arranging care for a child are determinations the coroner makes. A tool does not make them. National rules decide who may certify a death. EU data-protection rules cover medical details and living relatives. The file stores only what the coroner recorded, and interviews are not stored as audio.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the coroner is present under the judicial order and ends when the certification is on the file. The order itself is not created here.

The fields are the order reference, the time witnessed, and the coroner's certification. The coroner produces them by being present and certifying. A certification is not created for a death they did not witness.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on witnessing and certifying. Only the copy of the certification is shorter.
Upkeep is keeping the court's reference format on the file.
unknowns: Whether the court still wants the certification on paper as well as on the file.
Which judicial orders this office attends.
research_questions: Does the court still want the certification on paper?
Which judicial orders does this office attend?

already_counted.description: Certifying the death stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the court's reference format on the file

approvals.approved_version: certification the coroner made after witnessing the death

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the court still requires the certification in the coroner's own hand, the low end is the witnessing and the certifying, which stay, and the file copy is only a duplicate. Provisional, not a measured result.
